rules.rationale: Specs say "at most 2 decimal places" with "10.005" as the example. They do not say whether "1.500" (numerically 2 places, written with 3) is valid; the reference reads it numerically, the reviewer reads the written form.

rules.pattern: zero-quantized|quantized (annual|yearly) amount is zero|rounds to 0\.00|is 0\.00|collapse|loops forever|whole base|entire (remaining )?base
rules.rationale: depreciation_straight_line rule 8 loops while the remaining base is > 0 charging min(raw, remaining); when the yearly amount quantizes to 0.00 the rules never terminate, so the spec does not define the result.
prorata_billing rule 2: "Each entry is {date, monthly_price}"; it does not say whether extra keys are an "invalid entry shape".
fx_triangulation does not say what happens when two rate keys normalise to the same code (other than EUR).
xirr rule 11 says to raise when "no rate makes the NPV zero (no sign change ...)"; a double root makes the NPV zero without a sign change, so the two halves of the rule disagree.

rules.pattern: large|precision|significant digits|28|invalidoperation|scientific|quantiz|loses cents|loses tiny|many decimal places|exact remainder|remainder order|fractional-remainder|rounded decimal shares|1e\+30
rules.rationale: Inputs are only required to be finite (apr_apy: "There is no upper bound"; allocate_ratios: weights "may have any number of decimal places"; weighted_average_cost uses precision 50 "for divisions"). The reference evaluates under Python's default 28-digit context (or rounds a multiplication at 50 digits), so huge or very precise valid inputs crash with InvalidOperation or lose cents.
Dates must be "exactly YYYY-MM-DD"; the reference uses a regex with "$", which also matches before a final "\n".
idempotent_ledger rule 4: "key" and "account" must be "a non-empty string"; " " is non-empty, but the reference strips before checking.
weighted_average_cost rule 2: "any other type raises ValueError"; the reference raises TypeError for a list.
The formats are fixed digit patterns ("any other format raises ValueError"); the reference uses \d, which also matches non-ASCII digits.

rules.pattern: upper\(\)|length-expanding|expand|eur rate|eur entry|eur keys|eur also|bypass the eur
rules.rationale: fx_triangulation rules 3-4: codes are "exactly 3 letters A-Z" and "If EUR is present (in any letter case) its rate must equal 1"; the reference checks length after upper() ("ß" -> "SS") and lets a second spelling of EUR hide a non-1 rate.
